segments.narration: The survivors of this wreck were killed by each other. Not by thirst, not by the sea. By the man in charge.
On the fourth of June, 1629, the Dutch ship Batavia struck a reef off Western Australia with 341 people aboard.
About three hundred reached the coral islands. The commander took a longboat and sailed for help, three thousand kilometres away.
Behind him, Jeronimus Cornelisz took charge. A bankrupt apothecary, a junior merchant, and now the only authority for hundreds of kilometres.
He had roughly 125 people killed. Soldiers he had marooned fought back, and the rescue ship arrived mid-battle. Cornelisz was hanged.
